reason: (1) Non-genericity is not used. Model (u,r) maps the interval-base test to membership of x(P) in the affine preimage u^-2(I-r), which is still an x-coordinate set. The algorithm is group ops plus a membership test plus 2log2(p) bits of advice, so the generic-with-advice bound S*T^2 >~ r/|Aut| applies, and S=O(log p) buys nothing. (2) Weil/character-sum bound: for any affine image J of an interval, #{P1+P2+P3=0, x(Pi) in J} = |F|^3/N*(1+O(p^-1/2 log^c p)) uniformly over (u,r), because the incomplete sums of additive characters over x(nG) are O(sqrt p log p). So max over the p^2 models gives max/lambda -> 1, which rules out a p^eps gain. (3) Computed (cypari2, prime-order curves, k=8, 1500 models vs 1500 random equal-size subsets, counts normalised by |F|^3/N): p=4099: var_model 1.03e-3, var_null 1.29e-4, var ratio 7.9, KS p 7e-46, max/mean model 1.0998 vs null 1.0336, |F| CV 0.042. p=16411: var_model 2.38e-4, var_null 6.5e-6, var ratio 36.7, KS p 2e-87, max/mean model 1.0362 vs null 1.0083, |F| CV 0.021. Raw unnormalised var ratios of 136 and 473 come almost entirely from fluctuation in |F|. The proposal's 'false' prediction fails, because the variance ratio exceeds 1.25 and grows: random subsets are the wrong null, since structured x-sets carry Weil-sized correlations of relative size about p^-1/2, not p^-1. The 'true' prediction also fails, because max/lambda falls with p (excess 0.0998 -> 0.0362, about p^-0.73; relative sd 0.032 -> 0.0154, about p^-0.53, which matches the Weil scaling). Net: the gain is a log-factor at most, decaying to zero relative to lambda, so this is accounting only. It is the same 'variance' lever left open by the monodromy closure, but bounded by Weil rather than by monodromy.
